title: Java 8 / 17 — Mock Test
description: Test your Java knowledge with multiple-choice, true/false, and open questions extracted from the Java revision material.

questions.question: Which Java version introduced Lambda expressions and the Stream API?
questions.explanation: Lambdas, Streams and the new Date/Time API were all introduced in Java 8.

questions.question: What is the correct functional interface used by `Stream.map()`?
questions.explanation: `map()` transforms each element, so it requires `Function<T,R>`.

questions.question: Which method correctly creates an immutable list in Java 9+?
questions.explanation: `List.of(...)` returns a true immutable list; `Arrays.asList` is fixed-size but mutable per element.

questions.question: An `Optional<T>` can never contain a null value when created via `Optional.of(value)`.
questions.explanation: `Optional.of(null)` throws NullPointerException. Use `Optional.ofNullable()` for a nullable value.

questions.question: Which collector groups stream elements into a Map by a classifier function?
questions.explanation: `Collectors.groupingBy(classifier)` returns `Map<K, List<T>>`.

questions.question: What does `var` (Java 10+) do?
options: Declares a dynamically-typed variable like JavaScript
Declares a local variable whose type is inferred at compile time
Declares a variable that can be reassigned to any type
questions.explanation: `var` is local-variable type inference — type is fixed at compile time.

questions.question: Which of the following are TRUE about `record` types (Java 16+)? (Select all that apply)
options: Their fields are mutable by default
questions.explanation: Records are final, immutable, and cannot extend other classes (only implement interfaces).

questions.question: Which Stream operation is a terminal operation?
questions.explanation: `collect` triggers the pipeline. `filter`, `map` and `peek` are intermediate.

questions.question: A sealed class (Java 17) restricts which other classes can extend it.
questions.explanation: Sealed classes use the `permits` clause to control inheritance.

questions.question: What does `CompletableFuture.thenApply(fn)` do?
options: Transforms the result asynchronously when it becomes available
Blocks the current thread until completion
questions.explanation: `thenApply` chains a synchronous transformation; `thenApplyAsync` runs it in a separate thread.

questions.question: Which keyword in a switch expression (Java 14+) returns a value from a block?
questions.explanation: `yield` returns a value from a switch expression block.

questions.question: Which of these are valid functional interfaces in `java.util.function`? (Select all)
questions.explanation: `Iterable` has multiple abstract methods (well, actually only one — `iterator()` — but it's not in `java.util.function`).

questions.question: `Stream.parallel()` always makes the pipeline faster.
questions.explanation: Parallel streams add overhead. They help only on large data sets and CPU-bound ops with no shared state.

questions.question: What is the default method in an interface used for?
options: To provide a default implementation that implementing classes inherit
questions.explanation: `default` methods (Java 8+) let interfaces evolve without breaking implementations.

questions.question: Which Date/Time API class represents a date WITHOUT time zone?
questions.explanation: `java.time.LocalDate` represents a date with no time and no zone.

questions.question: Explain the difference between `==` and `.equals()` in Java when comparing two `String` objects.
questions.modelAnswer: `==` compares object references (memory addresses), while `.equals()` compares the string content. Two different String objects with the same characters can be `.equals()` true but `==` false. String literals are interned in the string pool, so `"abc" == "abc"` is true, but `new String("abc") == "abc"` is false.

questions.question: Which collection guarantees insertion order AND uniqueness?
questions.explanation: `LinkedHashSet` preserves insertion order while enforcing uniqueness.

questions.question: `String` is immutable in Java.
questions.explanation: Once created, the contents of a String cannot be changed. Methods like `concat` return new String instances.

questions.question: Which stream collector returns the first element matching a predicate?
questions.explanation: `findFirst()` returns an `Optional<T>` of the first matching element. `findAny()` may return any element (parallel-friendly).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `@FunctionalInterface` annotation?
questions.modelAnswer: It marks an interface as having exactly one abstract method, making it eligible for use with lambda expressions or method references. The annotation is optional — the compiler will still treat any single-abstract-method interface as functional — but the annotation makes the intent explicit and triggers a compile error if anyone adds a second abstract method.

questions.question: Which exception is checked?
questions.explanation: `IOException` is a checked exception (must be declared or caught). The others are unchecked (RuntimeException).

questions.question: Which of the following can a `record` do?
questions.explanation: Records can implement interfaces, define static members, and use compact constructors for validation. They cannot extend another class.

questions.question: What does `List.copyOf(list)` return?
options: A view of the original list
questions.explanation: `List.copyOf` returns an unmodifiable shallow copy. Modifying the source after copying does NOT affect the copy.

questions.question: Text blocks (Java 15+) preserve all leading whitespace exactly as written in source.
questions.explanation: The compiler removes incidental whitespace common to all lines (called 'incidental white space stripping').

questions.question: Which is the correct way to create a thread-safe HashMap?
questions.explanation: Both work, but `ConcurrentHashMap` offers better concurrent performance via segment locking.

questions.question: What is the difference between `Stream.map()` and `Stream.flatMap()`?
questions.modelAnswer: `map(fn)` applies `fn` to each element and produces a stream of the same size — each element is transformed one-to-one. `flatMap(fn)` applies `fn` that returns a Stream for each element, then flattens all those streams into a single stream — useful for one-to-many transformations like extracting all words from a list of sentences.
keyPoints: function returns a Stream in flatMap

questions.question: What is the result of `Optional.empty().orElseThrow()`?
questions.explanation: `orElseThrow()` (no-arg variant) throws `NoSuchElementException` when the optional is empty.

questions.question: Pattern matching for `instanceof` (Java 16+) lets you bind the cast result to a variable in the same expression.
questions.explanation: Example: `if (obj instanceof String s) { ... use s ... }`

questions.question: Which interface is the parent of `Set`, `List`, and `Queue`?
questions.explanation: `Collection` is the root of those three. `Iterable` is the parent of `Collection`.

questions.question: Why is the `final` keyword often used on local variables captured by a lambda?
questions.modelAnswer: Local variables captured by a lambda must be either explicitly `final` or 'effectively final' (never reassigned after initialization). This is because lambdas may execute on a different thread or at a later time, and Java needs to guarantee the captured value cannot change unexpectedly. Marking the variable `final` makes the intent explicit and prevents accidental reassignment.
